title: The bucket strategy: three buckets
objectives: Explain the three buckets, what each covers, and illustrative shares.
Say how refills work and why bad years don't force equity sales.
body_md:
Split the corpus by when the money will be spent, so a market fall never forces equity sales to pay this year's bills.

| Bucket | Covers | Typical home | Illustrative share of ₹1 Cr (need ₹4 L a year) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Income | Next 1–2 years of withdrawals | Savings, liquid or money-market funds | ₹8–10 L |
| 2. Stability | Years 3–7 | Short-duration debt, conservative hybrid funds | ₹20–25 L |
| 3. Growth | Year 8 onwards | Equity or balanced funds | ₹65–70 L |

How it works: the monthly SWP runs from Bucket 1. Once a year, refill Bucket 1 from Bucket 2, and Bucket 2 from Bucket 3, taking more from equity in good years and less in bad years. In a bad year, Bucket 2 keeps paying while equity recovers.
example: ₹1 Cr, need ₹4 L a year: Bucket 1 ₹8–10 L, Bucket 2 ₹20–25 L, Bucket 3 ₹65–70 L.
say: The monthly SWP runs from Bucket 1.
In a bad year, Bucket 2 keeps paying while equity recovers.
never: Run the SWP from the equity bucket.
Refill Bucket 1 from equity in a bad year.

o: The next 1–2 years of withdrawals in liquid funds
check.why: The next 1–2 years of withdrawals in liquid funds. The SWP runs from here.

o: Years 3–7, in short-duration debt or conservative hybrid funds
check.why: Bucket 2: years 3–7. Short-duration debt, conservative hybrid funds. ₹20–25 L.

o: Once a year from Bucket 2, and Bucket 2 from Bucket 3 — more from equity in good years, less in bad years
check.why: Once a year, refill Bucket 1 from Bucket 2, and Bucket 2 from Bucket 3, taking more from equity in good years and less in bad years.
